rootCause: src/domain/order-status.ts exports `OrderStatus` as a const object — it was an enum before the migration off enums, and an enum declares both a value and a type where a const object declares only a value. Four annotations across src/orders/board.ts, src/orders/filter.ts and src/reporting/summary.ts still use the name in type position.
expectedFix: Add a type beside the value, such as `export type OrderStatus = (typeof OrderStatus)[keyof typeof OrderStatus]`, or write `typeof OrderStatus` at the four annotation sites. The enum migration is the decision that settles all four.
purpose: The cascade with the LEAST material of any fixture here: four diagnostics sharing one cause, and not one of them carries a relatedInformation or a resolvable declaration — the name exists, it simply has no meaning in type position, so there is nothing for the source to capture. Where `missing-required-property` shows a link that is present but unused, and `assignability-mismatch` shows a link that is present and misleading, this one shows the third case: no link at all. Any future rule that folds it would have to work from `ProgramFacts.imports` and the identifier, which is precisely the 'same identifier' derivation §5.1 forbids. It is therefore the fixture that marks the outer edge of what the structural threshold can ever reach.
